tasks.title: Build full Agent Hub chat as primary agent UI
tasks.description: Build the proper Agent Hub chat interface and runtime that can eventually replace Codex CLI, Claude Code, Jenny chat surfaces, and other TUIs for interactive work. The core UX lives in Agent Hub, not SummitFlow. It must support real coding and agent work from the Agent Hub UI, while browser co-browse extensions act as lightweight clients of the same session.
done_when: Agent Hub has a full primary chat UI suitable for real agent work, not just simple prompts.
Chat supports streaming, stop, regenerate, continue, session resume, session fork/branch, and compaction.
Chat renders tool calls, tool results, errors, code diffs, artifacts, attachments, and long-running status clearly.
Chat supports project/task binding, agent selection, model/thinking controls, permissions including ask/allow/YOLO, context visibility, and cost/token hints.

Agent Hub backend exposes durable session/event APIs for browser-extension clients and other external clients to send messages, annotations, page-state events, artifacts, wake events, and permission/control events.
Browser-extension chat bubbles can attach to the same Agent Hub session and continue the conversation without copy/paste.
Codex CLI, Claude Code, Jenny, and other TUIs have a documented adapter/replacement path through Agent Hub sessions.
pi-mono-inspired concepts are evaluated and selectively adopted: event-first runtime, app-message vs model-message separation, artifacts, session tree, and simple extension points.
The implementation remains simple and performant: no broad plugin marketplace, no terminal emulation as primary UX, no high-volume browser telemetry in model context.

Focused backend/frontend tests pass through the project quality gate, and a demo proves starting in Agent Hub, doing agent/coding work, jumping to browser extension chat/annotation, and resuming in Agent Hub.

tasks.description:

- Relevant Jenny heartbeat acceptance/benchmark coverage stays green.

tasks.title: Canonicalize and harden Jenny self-improvement loop
tasks.description:
Objective: refactor Jenny self-improvement into one canonical, measurable, autoresearch-style loop owned by Agent Hub. Replace the remaining file-based honing prompt/runtime path with the canonical DB-backed prompt system, keep the evaluator protected, add real-heartbeat scoring as field evidence, and finish the UI-managed control surface so Jenny can improve herself without copy/pasted operator prompts.

Why now: the current improvement path is only partially fixed. We now have schedule control, trendlines, and recent runs in /persona/analytics, but the scheduled honing loop still relies on backend/scripts/persona_honing/_prompt.py and does not yet combine protected lab scoring with recent real-heartbeat field scoring. That leaves Jenny improvement split across old and new systems and violates the single-source-of-truth prompt mandate.

Principles / constraints:
- One source of truth for reusable Jenny improvement instructions: canonical DB-backed prompt(s) only. Delete the file-based prompt path rather than maintaining both.
- Follow autoresearch discipline: fixed protected evaluator, isolated candidate lane, baseline vs candidate comparison, keep on measured win, discard/rollback on real regression.
- Jenny may improve prompts, memory, config, and valid control-plane/runtime code as needed, but she may not rewrite the evaluator that grades the candidate inside the same improvement pass.
- Keep real Jenny heartbeats enabled. Improvement runs must treat recent real heartbeats as outer-loop field evidence, not replace production heartbeats with synthetic-only grading.
- Reliability is a gate with a small tolerance band; effectiveness next; efficiency/token efficiency as tie-breakers. Borderline promote/rollback decisions should escalate to supervisor review.
- Scheduled runs must skip on overlap instead of stacking concurrent self-improvement passes.
- Auto-commit/push valid wins. Avoid bandaids, duplicate rule stores, and Frankensteined wrappers. Fix sources, delete stale paths, and keep the simplest correct design.

Required architecture:
1. Canonical prompt path
- Create/use one canonical DB-backed Jenny improvement prompt and route scheduled/manual improvement through it.
- Remove runtime dependence on backend/scripts/persona_honing/_prompt.py and any parallel instruction store for this workflow.

2. Protected evaluation path
- Keep the evaluator/benchmark suite protected from candidate self-editing.
- Run each improvement in an isolated candidate lane/branch/worktree.
- Compare baseline vs candidate and promote only on measured win.

3. Field scoring path
- Score recent real Jenny heartbeats for reliability, effectiveness, efficiency, token efficiency, and truth/reporting quality.
- Feed that field evidence back into the improvement run and surface it beside the lab suite metrics.

4. Promotion policy
- Support tolerance-aware reliability gating.
- Escalate borderline cases to supervisor review, with supervisor override allowed.
- Defer/skip overlapping scheduled runs cleanly.

5. UX / management
- Keep /persona/analytics as the first-class management surface.
- Support enable/disable, cadence control (minimum 15 minutes), lab trends, field trends, recent runs, current risks, and enough detail to understand why a candidate promoted, held, or rolled back without forcing Arena-style scrolling.

Done when:
1. Scheduled Jenny self-improvement no longer depends on file-based prompt code and uses canonical DB-backed prompt records as the sole reusable prompt source.
2. The improvement loop runs baseline/candidate/protective evaluation in isolation and can auto-promote or discard based on protected metrics plus supervisor review for borderline cases.
3. Recent real heartbeats are scored and visible in /persona/analytics alongside the lab-suite metrics, and the improvement loop consumes that field evidence.
4. Schedule controls remain UI/API managed, overlap skips work correctly, cadence supports 15-minute runs, and successful candidates can auto-commit/push.
5. Tests, rebuild, and live UI/API verification prove the new flow end to end.

Verification:
- dt pytest for touched backend/API/workflow/script coverage
- dt --frontend-only --check for UI/API client changes
- rebuild.sh agent-hub after code edits
- live API verification for persona improvement endpoints
- live /persona/analytics verification showing both lab and field score surfaces
- at least one end-to-end improvement run exercising the protected evaluation/promotion path or a clearly documented dry-run equivalent if a real promotion is not yet safe

Scope / likely files:
- backend/app/workflows/persona_scheduler.py
- backend/scripts/run_persona_honing_loop.py
- backend/scripts/persona_honing/*
- backend/app/services/persona_improvement.py
- backend/app/services/_benchmark_config.py
- backend/app/api/persona/*
- backend/scripts/persona_benchmark_cases.py
- backend/scripts/persona_benchmark_persistence.py
- frontend/src/app/persona/analytics/*
- prompt records managed through st prompt, not hardcoded prompt files

Initial subtask breakdown:
- Canonicalize Jenny self-improvement prompt storage and routing.
- Add protected lab+field promotion logic with supervisor-borderline handling.
- Score recent real heartbeats and surface field trends in the analytics UI.
- Delete obsolete file-based prompt/runtime paths and tighten tests around the new architecture.
